info.title: AssetBase API
info.description:
**AssetBase** is an RFID/QR-driven asset-tracking and compliance product. One codebase,
two topologies: a **cloud SaaS** (AWS App Runner, `assetbase-api.ambivo.com`) and an
**on-prem appliance**. `DEPLOY_MODE` selects the topology and defaults to `onprem`.
AssetBase keeps its data in its own MongoDB cluster. It calls the **Ambivo Core API**
for authentication, the tenant user directory, AI vision (cloud mode only) and
Stripe-backed billing.

## Two refusals that are not about the caller's token

**A request that skipped the load balancer gets `404`.** On a partner cluster
every path except `/health` requires the `X-Ambivo-Origin-Token` header, which
the load balancer adds and a client never sets. It is armed only where
`WL_ORIGIN_TOKEN` is configured, so cloud and on-prem deployments are
unaffected. The body is `{"detail": "Not Found"}`. See the `OriginToken`
security scheme.

**A token carrying no module permissions cannot write to the register.** The
module is `installed_base`. A JWT whose `module_access` claim is absent gets
`403 FORBIDDEN` on a gated write, with a message naming the module and the
permission. A claim that does not name the module gets `403 FORBIDDEN` too.
Reads are not gated. `LEGACY_MODULE_ACCESS=true` lets a token with no claim
write again. It defaults to off.

The gated writes are: create, update and delete an asset, scan capture,
check-out and check-in, dispose and reinstate, creating or updating a
category or a lifecycle state, CSV import (`C`), enrolling audit exceptions
(`C`), and adding or removing a hierarchy edge (`U`). Scans, other audit
routes, files, labels, hierarchy reads and comments do not check module
permissions.

This spec documents the AssetBase API and the Core API endpoints AssetBase calls:

| Section | Host | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| AssetBase product API (register, scans, audits, files, labels, comments) | `assetbase-api.ambivo.com` | `Authorization: Bearer` |
| AssetBase auth proxy (`/user/*`, `/admin/sms/verifications`) | `assetbase-api.ambivo.com`, forwards to Core | none, except `/user/mfa`, which forwards the caller's Bearer |
| AssetBase local auth (`/auth/*`) | `assetbase-api.ambivo.com` | none |
| AssetBase internal billing jobs (`/billing/*` except `/billing/usage`) | `assetbase-api.ambivo.com` | `X-Internal-API-Key` |
| Core API — tenant users | `ingress.ambivo.com` (`AMBIVO_BASE_URL`) | `Authorization: Bearer` (forwarded) |
| Core API — vision (AI Identify / AI scan verify) | `goferapi.ambivo.com` (`GOFER_BASE_URL`) | `Authorization: Bearer` (forwarded) |
| Core API — AssetBase billing seam (`/assetbase/*`) | `ingress.ambivo.com` (`AMBIVO_BASE_URL`) | `X-Internal-API-Key` |

The Core hosts are the defaults. A partner cluster points `AMBIVO_BASE_URL`
(or `WL_API_BASE` or `WL_GOFER_API_URL`) at its own Core. `GOFER_BASE_URL` has no such
alias. A cluster that does not set it sends its vision calls to `goferapi.ambivo.com`.

## Response envelope

AssetBase JSON responses follow the platform standard:

```json
{ "result": 1, "installed_base": [ ... ], "count": 12 }
{ "result": 2, "error_code": "NOT_FOUND", "error": { "message": "Asset not found" } }
```

AssetBase returns a **real HTTP status** alongside `result: 2` (400, 401, 402, 403, 404,
409, 413, 429, 500, 502, 503).

Three kinds of response use FastAPI's `{"detail": ...}` body instead:

- request validation failures (a missing required query parameter, a body that fails
  the Pydantic model), with status `422`;
- the internal-key refusal (`401`) and the argument checks on `/billing/*`
  (`400`);
- the origin-guard `404`.

Many routes read a path id, or an id in the body, as a MongoDB ObjectId without checking
it first. On those routes an id that is not 24 hex characters answers `500` with a
plain-text body. The routes that check the id answer `400 VALIDATION`, and their
descriptions say so.

The **auth-proxy routes** answer HTTP 200 and carry Core's JSON body as it came, so
branch on `result` / `error_code` there. Two statuses pass through: a `429` from Core
(with its `Retry-After` header), and a `401` on `/user/mfa`. When Core cannot be
reached, or answers with something that is not JSON, the proxy answers 200 with
`error_code: AMBIVO_UNREACHABLE`. When Core did answer, `upstream_status` carries
its status.

Most payloads are keyed by **entity name**: `installed_base`,
`asset_audit_session`, `asset_audit_exception`, `asset_custody`, `asset_disposal`,
`asset_category`, `asset_lifecycle_state`, `audit_source`, `label_template`,
`scan_interface`, `comments`. `GET /audits/suggested-match-key` and the `/billing/*`
routes put their payload under `data`. List responses add `count`. Paginated
responses add `total`, `skip` and `limit`.

## Authentication — two modes, one header

Clients always send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; what the token *is* depends on
`DEPLOY_MODE`:

- **cloud** — the client authenticates against Ambivo Core (directly, or via the
  AssetBase auth proxy below) and sends **Ambivo's own JWT**. AssetBase validates it
  locally with the shared secret (`AMBIVO_JWT_SECRET`, algorithm `AMBIVO_JWT_ALGORITHM`,
  default HS256). No round-trip per request. With no secret configured every call
  answers `500 AUTH_MISCONFIGURED`.
- **onprem** — `POST /auth/login` verifies the credentials online against Core once, then
  mints an **appliance-local session JWT** signed with the appliance's own key
  (`SESSION_SECRET`). The session expires after `SESSION_TTL` (default 24 hours) with
  `401 SESSION_EXPIRED`. Signing in again needs Core. `OFFLINE_GRACE_DAYS` (default 14)
  counts from that sign-in and answers `401 OFFLINE_GRACE_EXPIRED`. It can only fire when
  `SESSION_TTL` is set longer than the grace window. An appliance provisioned
  for one tenant (`APPLIANCE_TENANT_ID`) rejects any other with `403 WRONG_TENANT`.

Service-to-service calls use `X-Internal-API-Key` instead, matched against a shared
`AMBIVO_INTERNAL_SECRET`. The two sides treat a missing secret differently:

- AssetBase's `/billing/*` jobs let every request through when no secret is configured.
  AssetBase also skips its own calls to Core when the secret is unset.
- Core's `/assetbase/*` endpoints refuse every request when no secret is configured,
  with `401 INVALID_INTERNAL_KEY`.

## The capture / administrative split

The handheld and the web register form both call `POST /assets`, `POST /assets/import`
and `POST /audits/{session_id}/exceptions/enroll`. A capture client sends
`X-AssetBase-Channel: capture` and is never gated for capacity. A request without that
header is treated as administrative and is gated. On `POST /assets` and on the enroll
route, a body carrying `client_asset_id` (the offline outbox's idempotency key) also
counts as capture. On `POST /assets/import` only the header counts.

## Idempotency & offline replay

These mutations take a client-minted key. A replay returns the original result and
writes nothing new:

| Key | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `client_asset_id` | `POST /assets` |
| `client_scan_id` | `POST /scans/batch` (per read; the server mints one when it is missing) |
| `client_event_id` | dispose / reinstate / checkout / checkin |

A `client_event_id` is looked up across all of the tenant's disposal events (dispose and
reinstate share one set) or all of its custody events. Mint a new one for every event.

`GET /assets?updated_since=<epoch>` is the matching **delta pull**: rows touched at or
after the caller's high-water mark, oldest first, plus `deleted_ids` for assets deleted
since then. Advance the mark to `server_ts` from the response.

## Large jobs

Work that can be large runs inside the request below a threshold and as a background
job above it:

| Work | Background when | What comes back | Poll |
|---|---|---|---|
| Register export | rows > `EXPORT_INLINE_MAX` (2,000) | `asset_export_job` with `status: running` | `GET /assets/export/{job_id}` |
| Register import | rows ≥ `IMPORT_BG_THRESHOLD` (2,000) | `queued: true`, `job_id` | `GET /assets/import/{job_id}` |
| Bulk QR minting | assets ≥ `QR_BG_THRESHOLD` (300) | `queued: true`, `job_id` | `GET /labels/qr-generate/{job_id}` |
| Label sheet PDF | labels > `SHEET_INLINE_MAX` (500) | `queued: true`, `job_id` | `GET /labels/sheet/{job_id}` (rendered in parts) |
| Audit reconcile | live assets in scope ≥ `RECONCILE_BG_THRESHOLD` (100,000) | `queued: true`, session `status: reconciling` | `GET /audits/{id}`, then read `meta.reconcile.state` |

## Data domains

- **AssetBase MongoDB** — `installed_base` (the register), `scan_interface`,
  `asset_audit_session` / `asset_audit_exception` / `audit_reconcile_run` /
  `audit_register_snapshot` / `audit_report`, `audit_source`, `asset_custody`,
  `asset_disposal`, `asset_hierarchy`, `asset_file`, `asset_category`,
  `asset_lifecycle_state`, `label_template`, `asset_tombstone`, the job collections, and
  the billing evidence collections.
- **Ambivo Core (omnilonely)** — the tenant, the user directory, the Stripe subscription
  and the quota. AssetBase reaches them only through the Core endpoints in this spec.
  There is no cross-cluster join on the request path, so AssetBase **pushes** the
  billable count to Core.

Physical assets are `installed_base` rows. They default to `installed_base_type="equipment"`
and `direction="purchased"`, and every create path sets `is_tracked=true`. AssetBase uses
the platform's `installed_base` field names. It adds the RFID layer (`rfid_epc`,
`last_seen_*`, `maintenance_state`, `lifecycle_state`, `condition*`).

## Scan pipeline

`POST /scans/batch` and `GET /assets/lookup?record=true` write only to `scan_interface`,
the staging table. A sync job then promotes those rows into `installed_base`. It runs
in-process every `SCAN_SYNC_INTERVAL` seconds (default 60) unless
`SCAN_SYNC_ENABLED=false`. `celery_app.py` defines the same job on a Celery beat
schedule for deployments that run a worker.

`POST /assets/{asset_id}/scan-capture` writes the asset directly and also records a scan.

```
handheld / fixed reader / phone camera
          │  POST /scans/batch      (idempotent on client_scan_id)
          ▼
    scan_interface  ──ScanSyncService (atomic claim)──▶  installed_base

    POST /audits/{id}/reconcile reads scan_interface and installed_base
                               └──▶ asset_audit_exception, audit_register_snapshot
```

tags.name: Service

tags.name: Auth
tags.description:
Login. In **cloud** the client uses the proxy routes and then sends Ambivo's JWT as
Bearer; in **onprem** it uses `POST /auth/login` and sends the appliance session.
The sign-in proxy routes take no Bearer; the credential is in the body. `/user/mfa`
forwards the caller's Bearer. Proxy routes answer HTTP 200 except for a passed-through
`429`, and a `401` on `/user/mfa`. Branch on `result`.

tags.description: Tenant user directory, proxied from Core for pickers (custodian dropdown).

tags.name: Assets

The register. CRUD, search, delta pull, lookup-by-code, disposal, custody,
depreciation, sightings, import/export and AI assistance.

Photos, documents and generated label images belonging to an asset. Bytes go to S3
when `DEPLOY_MODE=cloud` and `ATTACHMENT_BUCKET` is set, and are stored inline in
MongoDB otherwise. `STORAGE_BACKEND` (`s3` or `local`) overrides that choice when set.
The raw endpoint takes the Bearer in the header.

OriginToken.name: X-Ambivo-Origin-Token
OriginToken.description:
**Not a caller credential.** The load balancer adds this header; a client
never sets it.

On a partner cluster the compute runs on Railway behind a GCP load
balancer carrying Cloud Armor, and **the Railway origin is public and
cannot be made private** — the LB reaches it through an internet network
endpoint group, which needs a public FQDN to proxy to. So the WAF guards
the partner hostname while anyone can skip it and call
`wl-<slug>-<svc>.up.railway.app` directly. Measured against the CRM API on
2026-08-24: a SQL-injection payload was refused with 403 through the load
balancer and answered 200 sent straight to the Railway domain — same
application, same payload, WAF sidestepped entirely.

`Host` cannot separate the two paths, because the load balancer
deliberately sends the Railway domain as `Host`, which is exactly what a
direct caller sends. A secret the LB knows and the internet does not is
the only discriminator available.

**A request without it gets `404`, not `403`** — a prober learns the host
is uninteresting rather than that it guessed a real service and missed a
header. The comparison is constant-time, so a wrong token cannot be
recovered a character at a time from response timing.

**Armed only where `WL_ORIGIN_TOKEN` is set.** AWS clusters, local
development and docker compose are unaffected and behave exactly as
before. `/health`, `/healthz`, `/healthcheck` and `/ping` are exempt
everywhere: the platform probes the container directly, so a guard that
failed the probe would restart the service into a crash loop — a security
control taking the service down rather than protecting it.

BearerAuth.description: Cloud: the Ambivo-issued JWT, validated locally with the shared HS256 secret. On-prem: the appliance-minted session from `POST /auth/login`.

InternalApiKey.name: X-Internal-API-Key
InternalApiKey.description: Service-to-service secret shared by AssetBase and Core (`AMBIVO_INTERNAL_SECRET`). With no secret configured, AssetBase's `/billing/*` jobs let every request through and Core's `/assetbase/*` endpoints refuse every request.

Channel.name: X-AssetBase-Channel
Channel.description: `capture` declares a field client, which is never gated for capacity. Anything else (or absent) is treated as administrative.

Ok.description: Success envelope. Entity payloads are added under their entity key.

error_code.description: Stable machine code. Branch on this, and show the message. Common values: `NO_TOKEN`, `INVALID_TOKEN`, `SESSION_EXPIRED`, `OFFLINE_GRACE_EXPIRED`, `WRONG_TENANT`, `AUTH_MISCONFIGURED`, `AUTH_FAILED`, `MFA_REQUIRED`, `AMBIVO_UNREACHABLE`, `FORBIDDEN`, `VALIDATION`, `NOT_FOUND`, `BAD_CSV`, `BAD_MATCH_KEY`, `BAD_SOURCE`, `NO_SCAN_IDENTIFIER`, `BATCH_TOO_LARGE`, `EXPORT_TOO_LARGE`, `ASSET_CAPACITY_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, `ASSET_CAPACITY_UPGRADE_REQUIRES_SALES`, `UNKNOWN_LIFECYCLE_STATE`, `STORAGE_WRITE_FAILED`, `STORAGE_READ_FAILED`, `VISION_UNAVAILABLE`, `VISION_FAILED`.

Detail.description: FastAPI's own error body. Used for request validation (`422`, where `detail` is a list), the internal-key refusal, the `/billing/*` argument checks and the origin-guard `404`.

InstalledBase.description:
An asset. Mirrors the platform's `installed_base` schema; only the fields AssetBase
actually reads or writes are listed here. Timestamps are **epoch seconds (int)**.

tenant_id.description: always taken from the token, never the payload

client_asset_id.description: offline idempotency key. A replay returns the first create.

is_tracked.description: AssetBase-managed physical asset; forced true on create

asset_tag.description: Human-readable code the label prints and a QR scan reads. **Required on `POST /assets`** — with QR the tag *is* the identifier.

lifecycle_state.description: Key from the lifecycle pick list; defaults to `in_service`. A key the tenant does not have is refused with `400 UNKNOWN_LIFECYCLE_STATE`.

disposed_ts.description: set by dispose and cleared by reinstate

condition.description: good | minor_wear | scratched | dented | damaged | broken

condition_source.description: `operator` or `ai_scan`, as sent to scan capture

userid.description: owner, stamped so the platform's access filter can see the row

access_dict.description: record-level access; when empty on create it is set to `{"*": ["C","R","U","D"]}`

scope.description: What the audit covers. Only `scope.site_code` is read: it limits the register rows counted at open time and compared at reconcile time.

match_key.description: `rfid_epc` or `asset_tag`. Left out of the create body, it is `rfid_epc`. Sent as `""` or `null`, it is set from the register (see `/audits/suggested-match-key`). Reconcile overwrites it with the key that run used.

audit_source_id.description: "" = reconciled against the live register; `__all__` = every baseline combined

run_kind.description: `official` when the latest run compared against the live register, `simulation` when it compared against a baseline. Empty until the first reconcile.

disposed_scanned_count.description: disposed assets that turned up — counted here, never in `matched_count`

meta.description: `reconcile.state` is `queued`, `running`, `done` or `error`, with `reconcile.error` on failure. `snapshot` holds `rows`, `truncated` and `captured_ts`. `report` holds the error when the PDF render failed.

enrollable.description: Computed per row by the same rule `POST /audits/{session_id}/exceptions/enroll` applies. True for an unresolved `unexpected` row with no `installed_base_id` that carries an EPC, or a code in its `detail`.

Scan.description: One read. At least one of `rfid_epc`, `code` or `installed_base_id` is required.

code.description: raw asset_tag / barcode / serial for a QR or manual capture

installed_base_id.description: set when the device cache already resolved the asset

capture_type.description: `rfid`, `qr`, `barcode` or `manual`; when empty the batch `capture_type` applies

event_type.description: `receive`, `issue`, `transfer`, `audit`, `repair`, `dispose` or `move`. On promotion, `repair` sets `maintenance_state: under_repair` and `dispose` sets `lifecycle_state: disposed` without writing a disposal event.

reader_type.description: Defaults to `handheld` per read, so the batch-level `reader_type` applies only when a read sends an empty string.

custodian_userid.description: on a check-in, the custodian who returned it

lifecycle_state.description: the state this event moved the asset into

disposal_date.description: when it left (epoch); defaults to the time of the request

active_in_register.description: false when the asset is disposed

disposal.description: Disposed assets only, and only when a disposal event exists. The latest disposal event.

tags.description: Classification, e.g. `QR-tag`, `RFID-tag`, `main`. An image uploaded without `QR-tag` or `RFID-tag` gets `main` when no other file of that asset has it.

url.description: A presigned S3 link when the bytes are in S3 (fetch it with no Authorization header). Otherwise the API-relative `raw_url` path.

storage.description: `s3`, `local`, or "" for a row with no backend recorded

filters.description: The non-empty filters among `q`, `status`, `site_code`, `tag`, `maint`, `condition`, `asset_category`, `manufacturer` and `asset_tag`. `asset_ids` is not recorded.

total.description: rows matched when the job started

download_url.description: A presigned link, minted on each read, when `status=done` and the file is in S3. `""` otherwise; use `/download` then. `GET /assets/export/jobs` does not include it.

ready_parts.description: the number of the latest stored part

Selection.description: How the bulk label actions pick assets. `asset_ids` wins when it is non-empty, and the ids are used as sent, with no tracked or disposed filter. Otherwise `all: true` selects tracked, non-disposed assets through the filters below. With neither, the request is refused with `400 NO_SELECTION`.

ExportRequest.description: Filters for `POST /assets/export` and `/assets/export/preview`. Other keys are ignored. Disposed assets are always excluded. No filters selects every tracked asset.

AuditSource.description: Summary view. The stored `keys` and `key_meta` are omitted.

AuditReport.description: A stored audit PDF record. The bytes are not included.

HierarchyNode.description: A compact asset summary used by the hierarchy reads. A field the asset does not have is `null`. Deleting an asset leaves its edges in place. A node for a deleted asset has `null` in every field except `installed_base_id`.

LabelTemplateWrite.description:
Fields `LabelService.save_template` accepts. Anything else in the body is
**ignored silently** — there is no unknown-field error — so a misspelled key
leaves that setting at its default rather than failing.

⚠ The millimetre fields are `label_width_mm` and `label_height_mm`, NOT
`width_mm`/`height_mm`. This spec named the short forms until 2026-09-08;
a client following it got a template silently sized at the defaults
(63.5 × 25.4 mm) with no error to explain it.

Used for both create and update — update is the same call with a template id
in the path, so it takes the same body.

`show_brand`, `show_cut_guides` and `is_default` are read by truthiness. The
string `"false"` counts as true. Send JSON `true` or `false`.

fields.description: Which asset fields to print. Each entry must be one of `printable_fields` (from `GET /labels/templates`) or start with the custom-field prefix `cf_`; **anything else is dropped without an error**.

ProxyEnvelope.description: Core's JSON body, passed through. `AMBIVO_UNREACHABLE` (HTTP 200) when Core cannot be reached or answers with something that is not JSON.

RateLimited.description: Core's `429`, passed through with its body and `Retry-After` header. When Core's body is not JSON the proxy answers `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

get.description: Runtime config the Flutter client fetches at boot: the Mapbox **public** token, the brand name and the deploy mode (which gates AI Identify).

post.description:
Verifies the credentials **online** against Core `/user/login`, then mints an
appliance-local session JWT signed with the appliance's own key (`SESSION_SECRET`).
AssetBase reads the user and tenant from Ambivo's token without verifying its
signature, and does not keep it.

The route is mounted in both modes. In cloud mode `get_current_user` validates
Ambivo's JWT, so a session minted here is not accepted there.

Errors: `401 AUTH_FAILED` for refused credentials, `401 MFA_REQUIRED` when Core
answers with an MFA step, `403 WRONG_TENANT` on an appliance provisioned for another
tenant, `503 AMBIVO_UNREACHABLE` when Core cannot be reached. Any other Core reply
without a token, a `429` included, answers `401 AUTH_FAILED`. A reply from Core that
is not JSON answers `500`.

The session expires after `SESSION_TTL` (default 24 hours). `tenant_id` comes from
Ambivo's token, else from the request.

token.description: appliance session JWT; send it as Bearer

post.description:
Forwarded server-side to Core `/user/login`, so the browser and the handheld call one
origin. The Ambivo JWT in the response is what the client then sends as Bearer.

The proxy forwards the body, the query string, the `User-Agent` and one
`X-Forwarded-For` address. It picks that address by walking the inbound
`X-Forwarded-For` from the right past known proxy ranges. When
`AMBIVO_PROXY_SHARED_SECRET` is set and Core is on https, it also sends
`X-Ambivo-Proxy-Auth` and `X-Ambivo-Client-IP` for a public address.

HTTP 200 with Core's body, or `429` passed through. Core reads the body as JSON only,
and refuses any query string with `400 INVALID_REQUEST_FORMAT`.

The response depends on the account's second factors:

- none due: the login response with the session token;
- one active factor: the challenge for that factor, with `is_mfa_response: true`;
- more than one: `is_mfa_response`, `requires_factor_selection`, a single-use
  `pre_mfa_token` and `factor_list`. Continue with `POST /user/mfa/initiate`;
- none, and the tenant's policy requires one: `is_mfa_response`,
  `requires_mfa_enrollment`, `enrollment_token`, `userid`, `email` and
  `mfa_default_method`. Continue with `POST /user/mfa/enroll_gate`.

is_mobile.description: `true` or `"true"` asks Core for the longer mobile session

trust_device_token.description: skips the second factor on a device trusted earlier

post.summary: Send the MFA challenge for a chosen factor
post.description: Takes no Bearer. The `pre_mfa_token` from `/user/login` is the credential. Core sends the challenge for `factor_id`, which must be in the token's factor list. Core answers `401 INVALID_PRE_MFA_TOKEN` for a bad or expired token; the proxy passes that on as HTTP 200.

Takes no Bearer. On a correct code for a pending login challenge, Core returns the login response with the session token. `trust_device: true` also returns a `trust_device_token`. `action: resend` sends the challenge again and needs only `provider_challenge_id` and `userid`.

200.description: Core's body. Carries the session token on success.

post.summary: Set up a first factor during sign-in
post.description:
Takes no Bearer. The `enrollment_token` from `/user/login` is the credential. Core
sends codes only to a contact the account has already verified.

| `mfa_type` | Extra fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | none | the verified contacts to choose from |
| `email` or `sms` | `contact_id`, or the typed `email` (for `email`) or `phone_number` (for `sms`) of a verified contact | sends the code |
| `email_verify` or `sms_verify` | `provider_challenge_id`, `challenge_code`, optional `trust_device`, `device_id`, `os` | the login response with the session token |

email.description: a verified email of the account, typed; `email` only

phone_number.description: a verified phone number of the account, typed; `sms` only

get.summary: List the signed-in account's second factors
get.description: Forwards the caller's Bearer to Core `GET /user/mfa`. A `401` from Core comes back as `401`. Core sends that `401` with no body, so the proxy answers `error_code: UNAUTHORIZED`.

post.summary: Add or confirm a second factor
post.description:
Forwards the caller's Bearer to Core `POST /user/mfa`. A `401` from Core comes back
as `401` with `error_code: UNAUTHORIZED`.

| `mfa_type` | Fields |
|---|---|
| `sms` | `phone_number` |
| `email` | `email` |
| `sms_verify` or `email_verify` | `provider_challenge_id`, `challenge_code` |

Core asks for `password` when the account already has an active factor (`sms`,
`email`), or when the verify would replace an active factor of the same kind.

delete.description: Forwards the caller's Bearer and the request body to Core `DELETE /user/mfa`. Core asks for `password` unless the account has no password its owner could know. A `401` from Core comes back as `401` with `error_code: UNAUTHORIZED`.

factor_id.description: sms only; removes that factor alone

post.summary: Resolve a token to its user (proxied)
post.description: Exchanges an existing platform token, or a temporary exchange token, for the user record. Core answers `MISSING_TOKEN` without `token`, and `INVALID_TOKEN` or `TOKEN_EXPIRED` for a token it does not accept.
Forwarded to Core `/admin/sms/verifications`. `action` is `send_verification_code` (the default) or `verify_code`. A verify with `challenge_id` reads the account from that challenge.
Answers `{"result": 1}` and does nothing else. The client discards its token.
Not implemented. Always answers `NO_REFRESH` (HTTP 200, `result: 2`). An expired token means signing in again.

get.description:
Calls Core `POST /user/get_tenant_users` with the caller's own `Authorization`
header, and returns `{id, name, email}` per user, sorted by name, ignoring case.
`id` is Core's `id`, or `userid`. `name` is Core's `name`, or `first_name last_name`,
or the email, or the id. Users with neither `id` nor `userid` are dropped.

A network failure reaching Core returns an empty list with HTTP 200. Any Core
JSON object, including an error, is read for a `users` array; with none, the list
is empty. A Core reply that is not a JSON object answers `500`. Core's `401` has an
empty body, so a token Core refuses answers `500` too. The same call is made in
on-prem mode, where the forwarded Bearer is the appliance session.

get.summary: List assets (and the offline delta pull)
get.description:
Tracked assets only (`is_tracked: true`). **Disposed assets are excluded by default.**
Two ways to see them: `lifecycle_state=disposed` (or another disposal state) returns
that slice, and `include_disposed=true` returns live and disposed together.

Interactive listing sorts by `updated_ts`, newest first. `total` counts every row
matching the filters. In a delta pull `total` still leaves out disposed rows unless
`include_disposed=true`, so it can be lower than the rows returned.

`updated_since` (epoch seconds) turns this into a **delta pull** for the offline
device cache: rows touched at or after the caller's high-water mark, oldest first,
plus `deleted_ids` (up to 5,000 ids of assets hard-deleted since then). Advance the
mark to `server_ts`. A delta pull always includes disposed rows.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on name, asset_tag, barcode, serial_number, model_number, manufacturer, rfid_epc and asset_category.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: Epoch seconds. A non-zero value switches to delta-pull mode: rows with `updated_ts` at or after this value, oldest first, disposed rows included. Sending the parameter at all adds `deleted_ids`.

server_ts.description: advance the delta high-water mark to this

post.description:
`asset_tag` is required (`400 VALIDATION`). Body keys that are not asset fields are
ignored. `tenant_id` is always taken from the token and `is_tracked` is set to true.
`site_code` defaults to the caller's. Creating directly into a disposal state is
refused with `400 VALIDATION`; register the asset, then dispose of it. A new
`asset_category` is added to the category pick list.

**Idempotent on `client_asset_id`.** A body whose `client_asset_id` already exists
returns that asset. A clash on the tenant's unique EPC or model + serial index
answers `409 DUPLICATE_ASSET`.

**Capacity gate (administrative calls only).** Before anything is written, Core
`/assetbase/check_capacity` is asked whether one more asset fits:

- within the quota, unlimited, or externally billed: the create proceeds;
- over the quota and inside the unattended cap: capacity is raised through Core
  `/assetbase/set_capacity`, then the create proceeds;
- over the cap: `409 ASSET_CAPACITY_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, quoting the annual and
  monthly amounts. Retry with `confirm_capacity=true` to accept;
- beyond the published rate card: `402 ASSET_CAPACITY_UPGRADE_REQUIRES_SALES`.

Nothing is created in either refusal. When the capacity lookup or the rate card is
unavailable, the create proceeds. A failed capacity raise does not stop the create.

The create permission is checked first (`403 FORBIDDEN`), so a caller without it
never raises capacity. The capacity check runs before the body checks. A request
then refused with `400` or `409` may already have raised capacity.

get.summary: Download the register as CSV (legacy, synchronous)
get.description: Builds the CSV in memory and returns it as `asset_register.csv`. Disposed assets are excluded. Above `EXPORT_INLINE_MAX` (2,000) matching rows it answers `413 EXPORT_TOO_LARGE` and points at `POST /assets/export`.

post.summary: Start a register export (CSV or PDF)
post.description:
No filters means every tracked asset that is not disposed. **Always returns a job.**
Up to `EXPORT_INLINE_MAX` (2,000) rows the file is written inside the request and
the job comes back finished: `status: done`, or `status: error` with `error` set,
both with HTTP 200. A storage failure ends up in `error` too. Above that the job
comes back with `status: running`; poll `GET /assets/export/{job_id}`.

The file goes to S3 when S3 storage is in use. Otherwise it is stored in the job
record; fetch it through `/download`. A PDF row carries the asset's QR and main photo.
A PDF above `EXPORT_PDF_MAX_ROWS` (2,000) rows is refused with
`413 PDF_TOO_LARGE`. CSV has no row limit.

Other errors: `400 BAD_FORMAT` for a format other than csv or pdf, and
`400 NO_MATCHES` when no asset matches.
How many assets the same body would export, whether it would finish inside the request, and whether a PDF would be refused. Nothing is written.

too_large_for_pdf.description: true only when `format` is pdf and `total` > `pdf_max`

get.description: The tenant's export jobs, newest first. The entries carry no `download_url`.
When `status=done` and the file is in S3, `download_url` is a presigned link. When it is `""`, fetch `/assets/export/{job_id}/download`. A malformed id answers `400 VALIDATION`.

get.summary: Download an export through the API
get.description: The file bytes, read from storage by the API. `409 NOT_READY` while the job is not `done`. `502 STORAGE_READ_FAILED` when the S3 read fails.

post.description:
Reads the CSV header row for these columns: `name`, `asset_tag`, `barcode`,
`asset_category`, `rfid_epc`, `serial_number`, `model_number`, `manufacturer`,
`status`, `maintenance_state`, `install_location`, `site_code`, `currency`,
`warranty_end`, `end_date`, `purchase_cost`, `tags` (comma-separated). A `cf_<key>`
column goes into `custom_form_dict.<key>`. Other columns are ignored.

Each row updates the asset with the same `rfid_epc`, else the same `serial_number`,
else the same `asset_tag`. Otherwise it creates one. Matching covers every
`installed_base` row in the tenant, untracked and disposed rows included. An update
sets only the CSV's columns, so `is_tracked` stays as it was. A row with no name, EPC, serial
or tag is skipped, and so is a repeat of an identifier within one chunk of
`IMPORT_CHUNK` (1,000) rows. New categories are added to the pick list.

Below `IMPORT_BG_THRESHOLD` (2,000) rows the import runs inside the request. At or
above it the rows are staged and a background job promotes them; the response
carries `queued: true` and a `job_id`.

On an administrative call capacity is checked **once for the whole file, before any
row is written**, using the row count. `confirm_capacity=true` accepts a commitment
the response quoted. A request with `X-AssetBase-Channel: capture` is not gated.

Needs the create permission (`403 FORBIDDEN`). It is checked before the file is
read and before the capacity check.

200.description: Import result, or the queued job

post.summary: AI Identify — suggest register fields from a photo

get.description: One entry per date, for tracked, non-disposed assets whose `warranty_end` or `end_date` is at or before now plus `horizon_days`, already-past dates included. An asset with both dates in range appears twice, once per `kind`. Sorted by date, oldest first. Reads at most 100,000 assets.

days_remaining.description: negative once the date has passed

get.description: Tracked assets with `checked_out: true`, most recently checked out first, up to 1,000. Each carries `custodian_userid`, `checked_out_ts` and `due_ts`.

get.summary: Resolve a scanned code to one asset
get.description:
Resolves a code to one tracked asset by exact match on `asset_tag`, `barcode`,
`rfid_epc` or `serial_number`. `record=true` also writes the scan to
`scan_interface`. Pass `audit_session_id` to attach that scan to a stock-take.

**A disposed asset still resolves, with 200.** The response then carries
`active_in_register: false` and, when a disposal event exists, a `disposal` block.
With `record=true` the scan is recorded for a disposed asset too.

`404 NOT_FOUND` when no tracked asset has the code. `400 NO_CODE` for an empty `code`.

200.description: The resolved asset plus its lifecycle block

get.description: The asset and its lifecycle block. Disposed assets are returned here too.

patch.description:
Sets each body key that is an asset field. `installed_base_id`, `tenant_id`,
`created_by_userid`, `timestamp`, `is_tracked` and `disposed_ts` are ignored.
Any tenant user with update permission on the module may edit any asset.

A `lifecycle_state` the tenant does not have answers `400 UNKNOWN_LIFECYCLE_STATE`.
Moving a live asset into a disposal state answers `400 USE_DISPOSAL_ENDPOINT`; use
`POST /assets/{asset_id}/dispose`. A new `asset_category` is added to the pick list.

Moving a disposed asset to a live state is allowed here. It writes no reinstate event
and leaves `disposed_ts` set. Use `POST /assets/{asset_id}/reinstate` to keep the
history.

delete.summary: Hard-delete an asset created in error
delete.description: Deletes the asset, its file records and the stored S3 objects of those files, and writes a tombstone for the delta pull. A failed S3 delete is logged and does not stop the asset delete. Every hierarchy edge with the asset as parent or child is deleted. Audit, custody and disposal history is kept. To retire a real asset and keep its history, use `POST /assets/{asset_id}/dispose`. Refused with `409 ASSET_IN_AUDIT` when the asset appears in any audit snapshot or audit exception; `force=true` deletes it anyway.

post.summary: Record what the operator observed at the scan
post.description:
Writes the asset and a scan row in one call. Only the keys sent are written.

- `condition` sets `condition`, `condition_ts`, `condition_by_userid` and
  `condition_source`. A value outside the list answers `400 BAD_CONDITION`.
- `condition_notes` is cut to 1,000 characters.
- `location` sets `last_seen_location`, `last_seen_ts` and `last_seen_by_userid`.
  With `relocate: true` it also sets `install_location`.
- `custom_form_dict` keys are merged one by one into the asset's custom fields.

The scan row goes to `scan_interface` with the found `location`, or the asset's
`install_location` when none is sent. Pass `audit_session_id` to attach it to a
stock-take.

condition_source.description: stored as sent, e.g. `operator` or `ai_scan`; applies only with `condition`

relocate.description: also move the asset's expected home

post.description:
Sends the photo to GoferAPI `/vision/analyze/upload` (`mode=custom`, `tier=standard`)
with this asset's `name`, `asset_category`, `manufacturer`, `model_number`,
`install_location` and `description` as context. The serial number is not sent.
Returns a match verdict, a condition grade and the defects the model reports.

**Nothing is written.** To keep the values, POST them to
`/assets/{asset_id}/scan-capture` with `condition_source: ai_scan`.

`structured: false` means the model answered in prose.

Errors are the same as `POST /assets/suggest-from-image`, plus `404 NOT_FOUND` for an
unknown asset.

condition.description: "" when the grade is not one the register can store

post.description:
Sets the asset's `lifecycle_state` to a disposal state and `disposed_ts` to
`disposal_date`, and appends an `asset_disposal` event. The asset keeps its id, EPC
and files. Disposed assets are left out of listings and exports, and later reconciles
do not expect them. When `force=true` disposes a checked-out asset, `checked_out`,
`custodian_userid` and `due_ts` are cleared and `checked_out_ts` is kept. No check-in
event is written.

`lifecycle_state` defaults to `disposed`. A state the tenant does not have answers
`400 UNKNOWN_LIFECYCLE_STATE`. A state that is not a disposal state answers
`400 NOT_A_DISPOSAL_STATE`.

Other errors: `400 VALIDATION` without `reason` or with an unknown `method`;
`409 ALREADY_DISPOSED`; `409 ASSET_CHECKED_OUT` unless `force=true`.

Idempotent on `client_event_id`: a replay returns the first event.

force.description: dispose even though the asset is checked out

200.description: The disposed asset and the disposal event

post.description: Returns a disposed asset to the register and appends a `reinstate` event. The earlier disposal event is kept unchanged. `lifecycle_state` defaults to the state the asset had before its latest disposal, else `in_service`; a disposal state answers `400 VALIDATION`, and a state the tenant does not have answers `400 UNKNOWN_LIFECYCLE_STATE`. `400 VALIDATION` without `reason`, `409 NOT_DISPOSED` for a live asset. Idempotent on `client_event_id`.

200.description: The reinstated asset and the event

get.description: Every dispose and reinstate event for the asset, newest first. The asset id is not checked, so an unknown id returns an empty list.

post.summary: Check an asset out to a custodian
post.description: Sets `checked_out`, `custodian_userid`, `checked_out_ts` and `due_ts` on the asset and appends a `checkout` event. Errors: `400 NO_CUSTODIAN` without `custodian_userid`, `409 ALREADY_OUT`, `409 ASSET_DISPOSED`. Idempotent on `client_event_id`: a replay returns the first event before any of those checks.
Clears the asset's custody fields and appends a `checkin` event naming the previous custodian. `409 NOT_OUT` when the asset is not checked out. Idempotent on `client_event_id`.

get.description: The latest 50 custody events for the asset, newest first. The asset id is not checked, so an unknown id returns an empty list.

post.summary: Mint the EPC and return printable ZPL
post.description: Assigns a unique EPC when the asset has none, saves it, and returns ZPL for a Zebra printer. The ZPL writes the EPC into the tag's RFID inlay and prints the label (name, asset tag, serial, EPC, a QR of the asset tag, and a footer with the brand name and install location). The asset's `tag_status` becomes `printed`. `regenerate=true` assigns a **new** EPC even if one exists.

get.summary: Depreciation schedule and current book value
get.description: Computed on each call. `depreciation_method` must be `straight_line` or `declining_balance` and `purchase_cost` must be above zero; otherwise the answer is `applicable: false`. The schedule runs `useful_life_months / 12` years, rounded down and at least 1 (60 months when unset). Declining balance uses `depreciation_rate` percent a year, or `1 / years` when the rate is 0. The start date is `in_service_date`, else `installed_date`. `current_book_value` is the book value after the last full 365-day year since the start date, or `purchase_cost` before the first year ends.
The latest 25 `scan_interface` rows for this asset, of any capture type, matched by `installed_base_id` or by the asset's EPC. Sorted by `last_seen_ts`, newest first.
Oldest first. The bytes are never included.

post.description: `tags` is an optional comma-separated classification, e.g. `QR-tag` or `RFID-tag`. The asset id is not checked against the register. `502 STORAGE_WRITE_FAILED` when the S3 write fails.

get.description: The file bytes with the stored content type, served inline. The file is found by `file_id` within the tenant; `asset_id` is not checked. `400 VALIDATION` for a malformed id, `404 NOT_FOUND` for an unknown one. `502 STORAGE_READ_FAILED` when the S3 read fails.

200.description: The file, with its stored content type

post.summary: Make this image the asset's main image
post.description: Adds the `main` tag to this file and removes it from every other file of the same asset. The file's own asset is used; `asset_id` is not checked. The main image is the one a PDF export prints. `400 NOT_AN_IMAGE` when the file is not an image, `400 VALIDATION` for a malformed id, `404 NOT_FOUND` for an unknown one.

delete.description: Deletes the stored object, then the file record. A failed object delete is ignored and the record is still removed.

removed.description: number of file records deleted (0 or 1)

get.description: Comments live in the asset's `comments` array. Any user in the tenant may read and add them. Only the author may edit or delete one (`403 FORBIDDEN`). `400 VALIDATION` for a malformed asset id, `404 NOT_FOUND` for an unknown one.

post.description: Returns the new comment and the whole thread. `400 VALIDATION` when `comment` is empty after trimming.

user_name.description: stored on the comment as sent

patch.description: Author only. Sets `updated` and `updated_date` on the comment.

200.description: Removal count and the remaining thread

get.description: Alphabetical, up to 500. Active categories only unless `include_inactive=true`. `q` matches part of the folded name. `with_counts=true` adds `asset_count`: tracked, non-disposed assets whose category folds to the same name. The list starts **empty** for a new tenant. The CSV import adds every category it sees, and so does saving an asset with a new one.

post.description: **Idempotent on the folded name** (casefolded, whitespace collapsed). Posting a name that already exists returns the existing row. `name` is cut to 120 characters and `description` to 500. `400 VALIDATION` when `name` is empty.

patch.summary: Rename, re-describe or retire a category
patch.description:
There is **no DELETE**: assets store the category *name*. `{"is_active": false}`
retires a category. It leaves the pick list, and assets keep their value.

A **rename** rewrites `asset_category` on every asset in the tenant whose value
folds to the old name; `assets_updated` reports how many. A new name that folds to
another category answers `409 DUPLICATE_CATEGORY`.

`is_active` is read by truthiness, so the string `"false"` counts as true.

200.description: The category and the cascade count

get.description: Sorted by `sort_order`, then label, up to 200. Active states only unless `include_inactive=true`. Each call first adds any built-in state the tenant is missing. `with_counts=true` adds `asset_count` per state, counting every tracked asset. When some tracked assets have no `lifecycle_state`, it also adds `unmigrated_count`.

unmigrated_count.description: with_counts only, and only when non-zero

post.description:
Both booleans are **required** (`400 VALIDATION`):

- `expect_present`: should a stock-take expect to find this asset? When false, a
  register reconcile that does not see the asset records an `info` `state_conflict`
  in place of `missing`. A scan of it still counts as matched.
- `is_disposed`: is the asset out of the active register? Reconciles do not
  expect it, and scanning one raises a `state_conflict` exception.

`is_disposed: true` stores `expect_present: false`.

`label` (or `name`) is required and cut to 120 characters. `key` is derived from
`key` or the label: casefolded, each run of characters outside `a-z0-9` turned into
`_`, and leading or trailing `_` removed. When nothing is left the answer is
`400 VALIDATION`. `409 DUPLICATE_STATE` when the key exists. `description` is cut to
500 characters. A `sort_order` of `0` is stored as 500.

The booleans are read by truthiness, so the string `"false"` counts as true. A
missing boolean is refused. Any value that is present is accepted, `null` included.

key.description: derived from the label when omitted

patch.summary: Relabel, reorder or retire a state
patch.description: Built-in states (`is_system: true`) accept `label`, `description` and `sort_order` only. Retiring one, or sending `expect_present` or `is_disposed` for one, answers `400 SYSTEM_STATE`. An empty `label` answers `400 VALIDATION`. A `sort_order` of `0` is stored as 500. `is_active`, `expect_present` and `is_disposed` are read by truthiness, so the string `"false"` counts as true. `is_disposed: true` stores `expect_present: false`.

post.description:
Writes each read to the `scan_interface` staging table with `processing_status: new`.
**Idempotent on `(tenant_id, client_scan_id)`**: a read whose id already exists is
counted in `duplicates` and not written again. A read without `client_scan_id` gets
a new server-minted id.

A batch over `SCAN_BATCH_MAX` (25,000) reads answers `413 BATCH_TOO_LARGE`. Each read
needs one of `rfid_epc`, `code` or `installed_base_id`, or the whole batch answers
`400 NO_SCAN_IDENTIFIER`.

Per-read `site_code`, `audit_session_id`, `capture_type` and `reader_id` fall back to
the batch values when empty.

get.description: The tenant's staged reads, newest `ingested_ts` first. Each row is the stored document with `_id` returned as `scan_interface_id`.

post.summary: Promote staged reads into the register
post.description:
Runs one promotion cycle now, the same one the scheduler runs. It claims up to
`SCAN_SYNC_BATCH` (500) rows in `new` or `error` state with fewer than
`SCAN_SYNC_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (5) attempts, oldest first. Each claim is an atomic
`findOneAndUpdate`, so concurrent runs cannot process the same row.

The cycle is not limited to the caller's tenant. It processes the pooled database,
which holds every tenant that is not isolated, and the counts cover all of them. Any
signed-in user can run it. An isolated tenant is one listed in `ISOLATED_TENANTS`, or
every tenant when `DB_PER_CLIENT=true`. Its reads live in its own database, and no
job promotes them. A row left in `processing` by a failed run is not claimed again.

A row matches an asset by `installed_base_id`, then `rfid_epc`, then `code`.
A matched row updates the asset's last-seen fields and becomes `processed`. An
unmatched row becomes `unmatched`. A row that throws becomes `error`.

get.description: Newest `started_ts` first, up to 50. Archived audits are hidden unless `include_archived=true`. Deleting a closed audit archives it.

post.description: Opens a session with `status: open`. `expected_count` is the number of tracked, non-disposed assets in `scope.site_code` (or the whole tenant) at open time. When `match_key` is left out it is `rfid_epc`. When it is sent as `""` or `null` it is set from `/audits/suggested-match-key`. The value is not validated here; reconcile validates the key it is given. `site_code` defaults to `scope.site_code`, else the caller's. The server sets `tenant_id`, `status`, `started_ts`, `started_by_userid`, `created_ts`, `created_by_userid` and `expected_count`. Any other session field in the body is stored as sent.

get.summary: Which identifier a new audit should compare on
get.description: Samples up to 200 tracked, non-disposed assets (optionally in one `site_code`). When at least half carry an EPC the answer is `rfid_epc`; otherwise, including an empty register, it is `asset_tag`. The counts behind the choice come back too.
Named baselines an `asset_tag` audit can reconcile against, newest first, up to 100.

post.summary: Import an ERP CSV as a named baseline
post.description:
Parses the CSV and stores the list of codes, with a name and location per code. The
file itself is not kept. Column names are matched without regard to case or
surrounding spaces:

- code: `asset_tag`, `asset_code`, `tag`, `barcode`, `asset tag`, `asset id`, `asset_id`
- name: `name`, `asset_name`, `description`, `asset description`
- location: `install_location`, `location`, `site`, `room`, `bay`

The first row wins for a repeated code. `400 EMPTY_SOURCE` when no row has a code,
`400 BAD_CSV` when the file cannot be parsed. `name` defaults to the file name.

post.summary: Snapshot the register as a baseline
post.description: Stores the `asset_tag` of every tracked, non-disposed asset (optionally in one `site_code`) as a baseline, with each asset's name and install location. Assets with no tag are left out. `name` defaults to `Register snapshot <date>`. `400 EMPTY_SOURCE` when no asset has a tag.

get.description: The stored codes in import order, one page at a time.
Also the poll target for a background reconcile — watch `meta.reconcile.state` until it reads `done` (or `error`).

delete.description: A closed audit is **archived**: hidden from the list, with its data kept. `permanent=true` purges it. Any other audit is purged outright. A purge deletes the session and its exceptions, runs, scans, snapshot rows and stored report records. The report PDFs in S3 are left in place.

post.description:
Compares the session's scans with a baseline and writes exceptions, a frozen register
snapshot, a run record and a stored PDF.

- `match_key=rfid_epc` compares against the live register's EPCs.
- `match_key=asset_tag` compares against the live register's tags. With `source_id` it
  compares against that named baseline; `source_id=__all__` uses every baseline
  combined.

`source_id` with `rfid_epc` answers `400 BAD_SOURCE`. Another `match_key` answers
`400 BAD_MATCH_KEY`.

A scan matches an asset by EPC, `installed_base_id`, or a `code` equal to the asset's
tag, barcode, EPC or serial. A disposed asset that was scanned becomes a
`state_conflict` exception and is counted in `disposed_scanned_count`.

When the live assets in scope number `RECONCILE_BG_THRESHOLD` (100,000) or more, the
run goes to the background. The session comes back with `status: reconciling` and
`queued: true`; poll `GET /audits/{session_id}` until `meta.reconcile.state` is `done`
or `error`. Otherwise the run finishes inside the request with `status: closed`.
`503 RECONCILE_DISPATCH_FAILED` when the background run could not start.

An unknown `source_id` answers `404 NOT_FOUND` on an inline run. A background run
does not check it first; the failure shows only in `meta.reconcile`. Any failed run
leaves the session at `status: scanning` with `meta.reconcile.state: error`. The
session status is not checked, so a closed session can be reconciled again.

Exceptions are kept **per run** (session + `match_key` + `source_id`). Re-running the
same combination replaces that run's exceptions and leaves other runs' exceptions in
place. Each run that writes snapshot rows replaces the session's snapshot.

get.description: One row per (`match_key`, `audit_source_id`) the session was reconciled with, and its counts. Newest `ran_ts` first.
The session's `scan_interface` rows, newest `ingested_ts` first, with the asset's name when the row is linked to one. `limit` is clamped to 1–200.

get.summary: The register as it stood at reconcile time
get.description:
The register rows the latest reconcile wrote for this session, sorted by `asset_tag`.
Up to `AUDIT_SNAPSHOT_MAX` (200,000) rows are kept. `limit` is clamped to 1–500.

`scanned` / `disposed` filter the rows. The **Matched** list is
`?scanned=true&disposed=false`: a disposed asset that turned up is also stored with
`scanned=true`, and it is counted in `disposed_scanned_count`. `matched_count` leaves it out.
`total` counts the filtered rows; `total_all` counts every row.

**Scoped by default to the session's most recent reconcile run** (by `ran_ts`). A
session with no run record returns every exception row.

Pass `match_key` and/or `source_id` to read a specific run, or `all_runs=true` for
every run. A `match_key` with no `source_id` reads the **register** run for that key.
With `all_runs=true`, `match_key` alone returns every run with that key.

`type` narrows to one or more exception types (comma-separated). An unknown type
answers `400 VALIDATION`. `counts_by_type` covers the same run scope with the type
filter left out.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: comma-separated: missing, unexpected, misplaced, past_eol, state_conflict

counts_by_type.description: every type is present, with 0 when absent

post.description:
Creates one register asset per enrollable exception (see `enrollable`) and marks the
exception resolved. The new asset is named `Discovered asset ` plus the first 8
characters of the EPC, or the code. It carries the exception's EPC, or its code as
both `asset_tag` and `barcode`.

Only exceptions of `session_id` are enrolled. An exception id that is malformed,
unknown, from another session or not enrollable counts as `skipped`. When an asset
with that EPC (or tag or barcode) already exists, nothing is created; the exception is
resolved with a note saying why, and counts as `skipped`.

Refusals, in order: `400 NO_IDS` when `exception_ids` is empty; `403 FORBIDDEN`
without the asset create permission; `404 NOT_FOUND` when `session_id` is malformed
or names no session in the tenant.

**Capacity gate (administrative calls only).** The gate of `POST /assets` runs once,
before anything is written. It counts the distinct EPCs and codes the call would add
to the register. Two exceptions for one tag count once. When that count is 0 the gate
does not run.

- over the cap: `409 ASSET_CAPACITY_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, quoting the annual and
  monthly amounts. Retry with `confirm_capacity=true` to accept;
- beyond the published rate card: `402 ASSET_CAPACITY_UPGRADE_REQUIRES_SALES`.

Nothing is enrolled in either refusal. A request with `X-AssetBase-Channel: capture`,
or a body carrying `client_asset_id`, is not gated.

get.description: Every stored PDF record for this audit, newest first, without the bytes. Each reconcile and each regenerate adds a version; earlier versions are kept.

post.description: Renders the PDF again from the session's current snapshot and exceptions, and stores it as a new version.

get.description: The latest stored version, or the one named by `report_id`. When the audit has no stored report and no `report_id` is sent, one is rendered and stored first. `400 VALIDATION` for a malformed `report_id`, `404 NOT_FOUND` for an unknown one. `502 STORAGE_READ_FAILED` or `502 STORAGE_WRITE_FAILED` when S3 storage fails.
One UTF-8 CSV (with BOM): a summary block, then every exception of the session, then the frozen snapshot. Custom fields become `cf_<key>` columns.

get.summary: Export the audit as a workbook
get.description: Three sheets: Summary, Exceptions, Register snapshot. Custom fields become `cf_<key>` columns.

Same service and response shape as the asset comments. Comments live in the session's `comments` array. Archived audits accept comments too. Only the author may edit or delete a comment (`403 FORBIDDEN`).

post.summary: Add a comment to an audit
post.description: `400 VALIDATION` when `comment` is empty after trimming.

200.description: Removal count and the remaining thread

post.description:
Nodes are `installed_base` ids; edges live in `asset_hierarchy`. Each edge stores a
`quantity` (default 1) and a `position` for sibling order. An asset has at most one
parent per `hierarchy_type`, so it can sit in a logical tree and a BOM tree at once.
The edge stores `root_id`, `path` and `depth`, taken from the parent's own edge.
Removing or re-linking an edge does not update the stored `path` of the edges below
its child. After that, `ancestors` can list former ancestors, `tree` can leave out
grandchildren, and the cycle check can refuse a valid link.

A `quantity` of `0` is stored as 1.

Needs the asset update permission (`403 FORBIDDEN`). It is checked before the ids in
the body.

Errors: `400 VALIDATION` for a missing id, an unknown `hierarchy_type`, a self-link, a
malformed id or a link that would make a cycle; `404 NOT_FOUND` when either asset is
not in the tenant; `409 CONFLICT` when the child already has a parent of that type.

depth.description: 1 for a direct child of a root

delete.description:
Deletes the edge. With `cascade=true` it also deletes every edge of the same `hierarchy_type` below the child, in the tenant. The edges below are found by following `parent_id` links down from the child, one level at a time. The stored `path` is not used. `removed` counts every edge deleted. Without `cascade`, the edges below the child stay and their `path` is not updated.
Needs the asset update permission (`403 FORBIDDEN`). It is checked before the edge is looked up. A malformed `edge_id` is `400 VALIDATION`. An edge not in the tenant is `404 NOT_FOUND`.

get.description: The nested subtree below any node, children in `position` order. `type` is not validated; a value with no edges returns the node with no children.
The node's direct children of `type`, in `position` order.
The node's ancestors of `type`, read from its parent edge's `path`. An empty list for a root or an unlinked node.

200.description: Ancestors, root first, the direct parent last

post.summary: Which of these assets already have a QR
post.description: Splits a selection into asset ids that already have a `QR-tag` file and those that do not. Nothing is written. `asset_ids` are not checked, so an unknown id lands in `without_qr`, and `total` counts the ids as sent.

For each selected asset, encodes its `asset_tag`, else `barcode`, else
`serial_number` as a QR PNG and stores it as a file tagged `QR-tag`. An asset with
none of the three is first given `asset_tag` `AB-` plus the last 8 characters of its
id, upper-cased.

With `skip_existing` (default true), assets that already have a `QR-tag` file are
skipped. A selection of `QR_BG_THRESHOLD` (300) assets or more runs in the background
and returns `queued: true` with a `job_id`.

`502 STORAGE_WRITE_FAILED` when the S3 write fails on an inline run. A background run
records the failure in the job's `error`. With `skip_existing: false`, an asset that
already has a QR gets a second `QR-tag` file.

A grid of QR labels on A4, rendered through `template_id` or the tenant's default
template. Labels follow the order of `asset_ids`.

Up to `SHEET_INLINE_MAX` (500) labels the response **is the PDF**
(`qr-label-sheet.pdf`, with an `X-Label-Count` header). Above that it is **JSON**
with `queued: true` and a `job_id`, and the sheet renders in the background in parts
of `SHEET_PART_LABELS` (2,000) labels. Poll `GET /labels/sheet/{job_id}`, then fetch
each part or `/zip` for all of them.

Selected ids that match no asset are skipped. A background run can finish with
`rendered_labels` below `total_labels`, and a part with no matching assets is not
stored, so part numbers can skip. Read `parts[].part` for the part numbers.

Errors: `400 NO_SELECTION`, `400 NO_ASSETS` when nothing matches,
`413 SELECTION_TOO_LARGE` above `SHEET_MAX_LABELS` (100,000), `404 NOT_FOUND` for an
unknown `template_id`.

200.description: The PDF (small runs) or the queued job (large runs)

X-Label-Count.description: labels on the sheet (PDF responses only)

get.summary: Progress of a background print run
get.description: `rendered_labels` of `total_labels`, and `parts` as each one is stored. A part can be downloaded as soon as it appears. `400 VALIDATION` for a malformed id.

get.summary: Download one part of a print run
get.description: `404 NOT_FOUND` until that part is stored. `502 STORAGE_READ_FAILED` when the S3 read fails.

get.summary: Download every stored part as one archive
get.description: The parts stored so far, in order, as `qr-labels-<last 8 of job id>.zip`. `400 VALIDATION` for a malformed id, `404 NOT_FOUND` for an unknown one. `502 STORAGE_READ_FAILED` when an S3 read fails.
The tenant's saved templates, default first, up to 100. Also returns `printable_fields`, the asset fields a template may place on a label.

post.description: Saving a template with `is_default: true` sets `is_default: false` on every other template of the tenant.

get.description: The template a sheet uses when none is named: the saved default, or an unsaved built-in template with no `label_template_id`.

patch.description: Takes the same body as create and changes only the keys sent. `404 NOT_FOUND` for an unknown template.

post.description: Stores the file as base64 on the template; it is drawn on every label of the sheet. The file type is not checked, and a logo that cannot be decoded is left off the labels. `413 LOGO_TOO_LARGE` above 512 KB, checked before the template lookup. `404 NOT_FOUND` for an unknown template.

get.summary: Usage, price and the evidence behind them
get.description:
Backs the "Usage & Billing" screen in one call. Bearer-authenticated, scoped to the
caller's tenant.

- `counts`: recomputed now. `billable_count` is tracked assets not in a built-in
  disposal state (`disposed`, `sold`, `lost`, `stolen`, `destroyed`) and not in the
  legacy `status` values `disposed` or `cancelled`. Tenant-defined disposal states
  stay billable.
- `series`: daily snapshots in the window. A snapshot is written only when the count
  changes, and on the first of each month, so a gap means the count did not change.
- `trailing_peak`: the highest count in the window, carrying forward the last
  snapshot before it.
- `pricing`: priced from Core `/assetbase/rate_card`. `null` when the card is
  unavailable, when `AMBIVO_INTERNAL_SECRET` is unset, or when the card cannot price
  the count.
- `events`: the latest 100 billing evidence events.
- `integrity`: a check of the snapshot hash chain over the tenant's first 400
  snapshots.
- `capacity`: `known: false` when Core's quota is unavailable. Otherwise count
  against limit. When over and priced, it adds `quoted_monthly`, `quoted_annual` and
  `disposition`.

To read the quota, this call pushes the current billable count to Core
`/assetbase/report_count` with `source: usage_screen`. It writes no AssetBase evidence
row.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: bounds the series and the trailing-peak window

broken_at.description: the date of the first broken snapshot

rows.description: snapshots checked; 0 when the chain is broken

drift_days.description: snapshots in the window with non-zero drift

post.description:
Runs `tasks.reconcile_asset_billing` inside the request. For each tenant it writes
the day's hash-chained snapshot and pushes the count to Core. A tenant whose snapshot
for the day exists is not written again. A snapshot identical to the previous one is
skipped, except on the first of the month.

With `tenant_id`, only that tenant runs. Without it, the run covers tenants that have
tracked assets, narrowed to Core's `/assetbase/billable_tenants` when Core answers.
When Core does not answer, every tenant with tracked assets runs.

`401` with `{"detail": "Invalid or missing internal API key"}` for a wrong key, when a
secret is configured.

Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`. When either date is missing, the period is the previous
calendar month.
Idempotent per tenant per period: an existing statement is counted in `existing`.

Without `tenant_id` it covers Core's billable tenants. When Core cannot list them,
or the rate card is unavailable, nothing is written and `data.skipped` says why.

post.summary: Record the Stripe invoice a statement produced (internal)
post.description: Sets `stripe_invoice_id` on the statement whose period starts on `period_start`. An existing invoice id is not overwritten: the answer is `updated: false` with `reason: already_set`. A missing statement answers `updated: false` with `reason: no_statement`. Both come back as HTTP 200. A missing field answers `400` with a `detail` message.

200.description: Whether the invoice id was recorded

get.summary: Everything needed to answer a disputed charge (internal)
get.description: One tenant's billing evidence for a period, named explicitly by `tenant_id`. Read-only. Returns the statement and whether it still matches its hash, the period's opening, closing and peak counts, the daily snapshots, the evidence events in the period, up to 20 capacity changes up to the period end, and the chain check. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`. Missing parameters answer `422`; empty ones answer `400`.

post.description:
For each tenant, reads the term from Core `/assetbase/subscription_term`, plans the
renewal, and sends the notice or applies the re-rate through Core
`/assetbase/renewal`. `today` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) overrides the date the sweep runs as.

Idempotent per tenant per anniversary: the notice and the re-rate are each recorded
as an event keyed on the anniversary, and a recorded step is skipped.

Without `tenant_id` it covers Core's billable tenants. When Core cannot list them,
or the rate card is unavailable, nothing runs and `data.skipped` says why.

Called by `GET /users` with the caller's `Authorization` header and an empty JSON body. Core returns the tenant's individual (non-bot) users; a non-admin caller does not see deleted users. `get_only_bots: true` returns bots instead. The user fields follow Core's privacy filter. Core adds `email` and `phone` when the caller is a tenant admin. A non-empty result is cached for 10 minutes per tenant, with separate entries for admin and non-admin callers. AssetBase reads `id` or `userid`, `name` or `first_name` + `last_name`, and `email`. A call without a valid token answers `401` with an empty body.

401.description: No valid token. The body is empty.

post.description:
The upstream behind both AI features. AssetBase forwards the operator's Bearer, and
Core meters the call against the tenant's GenAI quota.

| AssetBase feature | Form fields sent |
|---|---|
| AI Identify (`POST /assets/suggest-from-image`) | `mode=asset`, `tier=fast` |
| AI scan verify (`POST /assets/{asset_id}/verify-image`) | `mode=custom`, `tier=standard`, `prompt`, `context` (the register record, without the serial number) |

Core refuses an upload over 40 MB in total with `413 UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE`. It answers
`429` with `TOO_MANY_IMAGES` (more than 8 files), `IMAGE_TOO_LARGE`,
`VISION_MONTHLY_LIMIT_REACHED`, `FREE_TIER_EXHAUSTED` or `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, and
`503 NO_VISION_PROVIDER` when no provider is up. A tenant whose account is not fully
approved gets `403`. A call without a valid token gets `401` with an empty body.

Other refusals come back with HTTP 200 and `result: 2`: `NO_FILE`, `EMPTY_FILE`,
`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `NO_PAYMENT_METHOD`, `VISION_ANALYSIS_FAILED`, and invalid-input
codes such as `INVALID_MODE`, `MISSING_PROMPT`, `INVALID_TIER`,
`PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `UNREADABLE_IMAGE` and `EMPTY_IMAGE`.

A successful body puts the analysis at the top level, beside `result`.

For how AssetBase maps these onto its own errors, see
`POST /assets/suggest-from-image`.

attributes.description: keys outside the vision contract land here

raw_text.description: present when the model did not answer in JSON

401.description: No valid token. The body is empty.

403.description: The tenant account is not fully approved.

error_code.const: Account Review Pending before this feature is enabled

get.summary: The AssetBase Stripe price and its tiers
get.description:
Lets AssetBase price a register without holding Stripe credentials. The endpoint
reads the active price of the `assetbase` Stripe product and returns it; it computes
no rate. The quantity floor and the self-service ceiling are read from the price
metadata.

Test or live mode: `is_debug` decides when sent (any value but `false`, `0` or `no`
means test). Otherwise the tenant's own Stripe customer decides, defaulting to
**test** when unknown. With neither parameter it reads the test card. When more than
one price is active, the **oldest** is used.

Each tier carries `up_to`, `unit_amount_decimal` and `flat_amount_decimal`. There is no
integer `unit_amount`. `metadata` is the price's whole metadata object.

Errors: `404 TENANT_NOT_FOUND`, `503 ASSETBASE_PRODUCT_NOT_CONFIGURED`,
`503 ASSETBASE_PRICE_NOT_FOUND`, `500 SERVER_ERROR`.

parameters.name: is_debug
parameters.description: force test or live instead of deriving it

get.summary: What the tenant may hold, and whether N more would fit
get.description:
**Read only.** It writes no count, calls no Stripe API and changes no quota.
AssetBase calls it before an administrative create, import or audit enroll.

`count` is the last count mirrored by `report_count`. `limit` is the tenant's
`asset_records_limit` quota. The tenant is treated as unlimited when `limit` is `-1`
or `billing_external` is true. Then `remaining` is `-1` and `over_limit` and
`would_exceed` are false.

Errors: `400 MISSING_TENANT_ID`, `400 INVALID_ADDITIONAL`, `404 TENANT_NOT_FOUND`,
`500 SERVER_ERROR`.

needed.description: count + additional, with a negative additional counted as 0

post.summary: Mirror the billable asset count onto the tenant
post.description:
Core writes `{count, ts}` to `tenant.record_metrics_dict.asset_metric` with a
dot-path `$set`, so sibling counters are untouched. It then returns the tenant's
quota on the same call. The count is written for every tenant, externally billed
ones included.

AssetBase pushes the count after creates, updates, deletes, imports, disposals,
reinstatements, audit enrolment, the nightly reconcile and each usage-screen load.
On the AssetBase side a failed push is logged and does not fail the request.

Errors: `400 INVALID_JSON`, `400 MISSING_TENANT_ID`, `400 INVALID_COUNT`,
`404 TENANT_NOT_FOUND`, `500 SERVER_ERROR`.

200.description: The mirrored count and the resolved quota

post.description:
Sets a new quantity on the tenant's AssetBase Stripe subscription item. It only
raises:

- **Never for an externally billed tenant**: `409 BILLING_EXTERNAL`.
- **Never without a Stripe customer**: `409 NO_STRIPE_CUSTOMER`.
- **Never creates a subscription.** No active AssetBase item answers
  `409 NO_ASSETBASE_SUBSCRIPTION`.
- **Never lowers.** A quantity at or below the current one answers
  `409 NOT_AN_INCREASE`, with the current quantity in `data.quantity`.
- **Stripe computes the price.** Only a quantity is sent.

The change is prorated (`create_prorations`). AssetBase writes its consent row
(`asset_capacity_change`) only after this returns success. `trigger` is logged only.

Other errors: `400 INVALID_JSON`, `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, `404 TENANT_NOT_FOUND`,
`500 SERVER_ERROR`.

get.summary: Tenants that have purchased AssetBase capacity
get.description: Ids of tenants whose `asset_records_limit` is above 0. The nightly reconcile intersects this list with the tenants that have tracked assets. When this call fails, the reconcile runs every tenant with tracked assets. A statement or renewal run for all tenants writes nothing then. A reconcile, statement or renewal run for one `tenant_id` does not call it.

Read only. The AssetBase subscription has a monthly Stripe interval, so Core derives
the annual term from the subscription's start date. `anniversary` is the next
anniversary, and it stays current for 7 days after it passes.

A tenant with no Stripe customer, or no active AssetBase subscription, answers
`active: false` with a `reason`.

Errors: `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, `404 TENANT_NOT_FOUND`, `500 SERVER_ERROR`.

post.summary: Send the renewal notice, or apply the re-rate
post.description:
Separate from `set_capacity`, which never lowers a quantity. An externally billed
tenant answers `409 BILLING_EXTERNAL` for both actions.

- `action: notify`: queues the renewal email. Recipients are the Stripe billing
  email, the tenant's `contact_us_email` and `default_opportunity_notify_email`, and
  the configured internal address. `notified` is false when there is no recipient
  or the email could not be queued.
- `action: apply`: sets the new quantity with no proration. The checks run in this
  order. Outside 1 day before to 7 days after `anniversary` it answers
  `409 OUTSIDE_RENEWAL_WINDOW`. Without a Stripe customer it answers
  `409 NO_STRIPE_CUSTOMER`. Without an active subscription it answers
  `409 NO_ASSETBASE_SUBSCRIPTION`. A quantity of 0 or less answers
  `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; a missing or non-integer quantity counts as 0. A quantity
  above the current one answers `409 RENEWAL_CANNOT_RAISE`. The same quantity
  answers `unchanged: true`.

Other errors: `400 INVALID_JSON`, `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, `404 TENANT_NOT_FOUND`,
`500 SERVER_ERROR`.

200.description: Notice queued, or the re-rated item
